artifacts.title: Suspected neurological conditions: recognition and referral
assertions: Cervical radiculopathy referral assessment includes gait disturbance, clumsy or weak hands or legs and new bladder or bowel disturbance.
The 2023 update remains the current published NICE version; runtime does not infer a cervical diagnosis.

artifacts.title: ACR Appropriateness Criteria: Cervical Pain or Cervical Radiculopathy
assertions: The current revised-2024 document distinguishes acute or increasing pain, radiculopathy, trauma, infection, malignancy and prior cervical surgery contexts.
The source supports collecting imaging-pathway context but is not used by runtime to order imaging or diagnose.

artifacts.title: Meningococcal Disease Symptoms and Complications
assertions: Meningitis symptoms can include fever, headache, stiff neck, confusion, nausea or vomiting and photophobia.
Meningococcal disease can worsen rapidly and requires immediate medical attention.

artifacts.publisher: East Kent Hospitals University NHS Foundation Trust
artifacts.title: Neck pain / injury: aftercare advice
assertions: The July 2026 patient leaflet separates weakness, walking or balance difficulty, electric-shock sensation and bladder or bowel loss as urgent warning features.
The leaflet explicitly requests accessibility, interpreter and alternative-format needs, supporting a distinct handoff Fact.

artifacts.title: STOM neck-pain terminology and MRCM lookup
assertions: Build-time lookup confirmed active Neck pain (finding) 81680005, Cervical radiculopathy (disorder) 54404000 and Neck stiffness (finding) 161882006 with Korean descriptions.
MRCM lookup for Neck pain returned Severity 246112005 and Finding site 363698007 among allowed attributes; terminology does not determine urgency or diagnosis.

artifacts.title: STOM LOINC verification for atomic current pain score
assertions: FHIR CodeSystem lookup confirmed LOINC 72514-3 as Pain severity - 0-10 verbal numeric rating [Score] - Reported in version 2.82.
Only the atomic current pain score uses this equivalent mapping; worst pain and composite pain questions do not inherit it.
